Subject: MAP kickoff — initial scope & questions

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Priya and I regrouped and sketched a rough MAP. Before we lock timelines we need to align on the measurable success signals for the evaluation and the exit gates that will trigger either cutover or rollback. High-level asks: 

- Can you send your MAP template and a proposed set of acceptance tests that map to the success signals (quality, latency, false-positive rate for PHI redaction)?
- We need a recommended smoke-test schedule for the pilot (daily sanity checks + weekly runs).
- Please call out any blockers that would delay a production decision (SLA, audit evidence, model quantization regressions).

I attached a short list of our initial questions (Medisync_MAP_questions.docx). Target: 6-week pilot starting Oct 4.

Would you and your engineering lead be available for a 30-min alignment tomorrow?

Thanks,
Eric Tan
Director, ML Ops
Medisync Health

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Eric Tan <eric.tan@medisync.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@medisync.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18 11:02 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — initial scope & questions

Hi Eric / Priya,

Great to hear you reconvened. We can run the 6-week pilot but want to be explicit about the checkpoints so there are no surprises. Attached is our MAP template (VZ_MAP_template.xlsx) — I filled in the high-level milestones and a starter set of acceptance tests. Key proposals: 

1) Success signals (must pass to progress to next stage):
   - Functional: end-to-end throughput >= 12 r/s for 90th pct within pilot-requested load pattern
   - Latency: median generation latency < 350ms for 512-token requests
   - Quality: automated labeling concordance >= 88% on a 500-sample prompt set
   - Safety/PII: PHI-redaction false positive rate < 2% and recall > 98% on curated test corpus

2) Exit gates (hard stop if unmet by week 5):
   - Failed to meet quality threshold after two remediation sprints
   - Required audit artifacts (audit logs + KMS attestations) not provided by week 4

3) Acceptance tests (examples):
   - Concordance test suite (500 curated prompts) — pass if >=88%
   - Load soak (48-hour at anticipated burst pattern) — no OOMs or degradation of >25% in throughput
   - Security smoke (sample audit log retrieval + encryption verification) — no missing events

We can review tomorrow at 10:00am PT; Marissa will walk through the success matrix and Sean will cover smoke-test automation.

Next steps: I'll share the editable MAP and update the HubSpot deal (HB-4381) with the timeline.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: VZ_MAP_template.xlsx (xlsx)

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-19 08:18 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — initial scope & questions

Vanessa / Sean — attaching a compact success_matrix.csv with explicit signal-to-test mapping. Highlights below (pulling the most consequential items to discuss with Medisync):

- Quality signal mapping:
  * Metric: label concordance on sampled set (n=500)
  * Test: automated concordance job + manual spot check (20 cases)
  * Pass threshold: >= 88% concordance and no critical failures in manual review

- Latency/throughput gating:
  * Metric: 90th pct latency and p95 during synthetic replay
  * Test: replay with production-weighted traces, measured over 24h soak
  * Pass threshold: p95 < 500ms, throughput degradation < 20% from nominal

- Security/audit gating:
  * Evidence: continuous audit log stream for inference requests, KMS key rotation logs, SOC2-relevant artifacts
  * Test: sample retrieval of logs + checklist validation by our compliance engineer

Edge cases we should raise in the meeting: model quantization profiles can change quality slightly; propose a short A/B rollback path (keep a float32 variant behind a feature flag if we see regressions).

Attachment: success_matrix.csv (csv)

Marissa
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

--

Eric,

Quick technical note on rollback/variant pinning:
- We can expose a traffic-split feature flag at the route level. Rolling back to the previous variant is typically a 5–15 minute operation (configuration change + deployment of routing rule).
- Recommend we add a smoke-test that validates behavioral parity for a 100-sample golden set immediately after any rollback.

I've dropped a short smoke_test_plan.md in the Drive folder (checks: request/response checksum, latency regression, and audit event presence).

—Sean
